title: sklearn model logging: skops_trusted_types must list sklearn.tree._tree.Tree for tree-based models such as RandomForest
answers: Logging a scikit-learn RandomForest model with skops fails or is rejected when loading, what do I pass?
How do I register a sklearn model in the model registry with trusted skops types?
Where is the skops_trusted_types option for mlflow.sklearn.log_model handled and documented?
Which types need to be trusted when saving a sklearn tree-based model with skops?
body:
Path: mlflow/tracking/_model_registry/fluent.py:register_model is the docstring example that logs a scikit-learn RandomForestRegressor with mlflow.sklearn.log_model and then registers it. Sklearn model logging (save/log/register flows) passes a skops_trusted_types list through log_model.
Rule: For tree-based sklearn estimators logged through mlflow.sklearn.log_model, pass skops_trusted_types=["sklearn.tree._tree.Tree"] alongside signature and name. The example in register_model was updated this way, so copy that pattern when writing new sklearn examples or docs that log tree models.
Constraints: Stated for RandomForest-style examples in the diff; the PR does not show which other estimators need the argument, so check the skops error for other model types. Applies only when skops serialization is used for sklearn logging.
applies: Sklearn model logging examples and docs that use skops-based serialization for tree models.
says: Registering a random forest model in the model registry fails with untrusted type errors.
Loading a registered decision tree model fails because internal tree types are not trusted.
Update model registry tutorial examples for tree-based models to include necessary trusted types.
Saving a tree estimator with secure serialization fails during the model registration flow.
Allow users to register random forest models without running into serialization trust errors.
search: When logging tree-based scikit-learn estimators such as RandomForestRegressor using skops serialization in mlflow.sklearn.log_model, skops_trusted_types must explicitly include sklearn.tree._tree.Tree. This pattern is documented in the mlflow/tracking/_model_registry/fluent.py:register_model example and should be followed when authoring documentation and examples for sklearn model registration. The requirement applies specifically to skops-based serialization flows for tree models and does not specify requirements for non-tree estimators.
